identity.title: Envisioning Beyond the Pixels: Benchmarking Reasoning-Informed Visual Editing

problem.claim: Evaluate visual editing models on edits requiring temporal, causal, spatial, and logical reasoning.

gap.claim: Existing models struggle with complex instructions, appearance consistency, and flexible inputs in general visual editing.

contributions.claim: RISEBench, presented as the first benchmark for reasoning-informed visual editing.
A framework assessing instruction reasoning, appearance consistency, and visual plausibility using human judges and LMM-as-a-judge.
The authors report releasing RISEBench code and data.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish RISEBench as the first benchmark specifically for reasoning-informed visual editing.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors evaluated nine open-source and proprietary visual editing models.
The authors report that current models face significant challenges on reasoning-based editing tasks.
The authors report that GPT-image-1, the strongest evaluated model, achieved 28.8% accuracy.

narrative_sequence.summary: The abstract identifies persistent difficulties in general visual editing, including complex instructions and consistency.
The authors introduce RISEBench to study reasoning-informed visual editing across four reasoning categories.
They curate category-specific test cases and score reasoning, consistency, and plausibility with human and LMM judges.
Experiments on nine models reveal substantial challenges; the authors report 28.8% accuracy for GPT-image-1 and release code and data.

source_observation.claim: The benchmark separates evaluation into reasoning, appearance consistency, and visual plausibility, while covering four reasoning categories.

lessons.interpretation: Decomposing a compound capability can reveal whether failures arise from instruction interpretation, preservation, or output quality.
lessons.application: For a new multimodal benchmark, define orthogonal capability dimensions and report them separately alongside any aggregate score.
lessons.exception: This decomposition may be unsuitable when dimensions cannot be judged independently or when the target task has a single indivisible outcome.

unknowns: The abstract does not define the 28.8% accuracy metric, task distribution, or benchmark size.
It does not report agreement between human and LMM judges, per-category results, or evaluation conditions.
